slides.title: A one-minute reset

kind.text: Feet flat, hands resting in your lap. Let your shoulders drop away from your ears.
Breathe in slowly through your nose while you count to four.
Hold the breath gently, without strain, for another count of four.
Let the air out through your mouth for a count of six. Repeat three times.

slides.title: A healthy day

kind.text: A healthy day, hour by hour
Adjust your chair and screen before you open email. Two minutes now saves an aching neck later.
Stand up, refill your water and look out of a window on the way.
Take lunch away from your desk. A ten-minute walk after eating helps the afternoon dip.
Three desk stretches: neck, shoulders and a seated twist.
Close the laptop, write tomorrow's first task down and let the day end.

kind.text: Big changes fade when motivation dips. A habit so small it feels silly, like one stretch after each meeting, survives busy weeks.

slides.title: Bonus: the 20-20-20 rule
slides.notes: The 20-20-20 rule explained.

kind.alt: A person resting their eyes by looking out of a window

kind.text:
Every 20 minutes
look 20 feet (6 m) away
for 20 seconds
Focusing close up all day tires the small muscles in your eyes. Looking far away lets them relax. Blink a few times too.

glossary.definition: Fitting the workspace to the person: chair, desk, screen and tools set up so your body stays comfortable.
A pause of one to five minutes to stand, stretch, look away or breathe.
Every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet (about 6 metres) away for 20 seconds.
Breathing in, holding and breathing out to a steady count, such as 4-4-6, to calm the body.
